evidence: The original spawner used `std::env::var(RSS_LIMIT_ENV).ok()`, which maps VarError::NotUnicode to None and so to the default budget, contradicting the doc comment's 'malformed → Err'. e322618 matches NotPresent and NotUnicode separately.
guidance_note: When a function's contract says 'malformed → Err', check that every reader feeding it keeps 'absent' and 'present but unreadable' apart; an `.ok()` merges them.

evidence: Rust `s.trim().parse::<u64>()` accepts `+10` and `007`, while TS's `String(mb) !== raw.trim()` rejects them, so the spawner launched daemons that then refused to boot. The agent defined a new shared grammar that accepts 007 on both sides and rejects + on both, which is neither of the reviewer's options. It kept `trim` on both sides and called the result 'verbatim', and F22 later showed the two trims differ.
guidance_note: When a parser is claimed to mirror another runtime's, list each primitive both sides call (trim, parse, digit class) and confirm each one has the same semantics, rather than matching only the documented accept/reject cases.

evidence: No test covered log.ts. The agent deleted closeLog (F12) and added test/daemon-log.test.ts, which pins the surviving contract: the line is on disk on return, and rotation works. Its test duplicated the MAX_BYTES literal, which became F21.
guidance_note: When a new test needs a module's constant, export the constant instead of re-declaring the literal.

evidence: `mb * HEAP_CAP_OVER_RSS` is an unchecked u64 multiply on any parsed u64. The plan said checked_mul, but e322618 instead bounds the grammar at 2^53−1 so the product is < 2^54. That is a sound alternative, and the 99999999999999999999 vector pins it.

The RSS backstop is a 60 s poll and the heap cap is enforced continuously, so 'always fires first' was an overstatement. e322618 rewrote the README and the limits.ts comment to name the residual burst case.
guidance_note: Don't write 'always' about the ordering of a polled check against a continuously enforced limit; state the poll window as the condition.

evidence: Originally the env parse ran inside armLimits, after resetSpawnBackoff in onListening, so each malformed-env crash cleared the backoff streak. Moving the parse to the top of runDaemon in e322618 removes that ordering.
guidance_note: When a function changes from defaulting to throwing, trace every caller to find where in the boot sequence the throw now lands and which side effects have already run.

evidence: This is the same TS/Rust grammar divergence as F2, with the same concrete 007 crash-loop. The reviewer proposed a round-trip check in Rust; the agent unified both sides on a new digits-only grammar instead.

The 'daemon up heapCap=…' line and the lease were written before armLimits threw on a malformed env. e322618 moved the parse to the top of runDaemon. That turned it into a synchronous throw caught by index.ts's try/catch, which bypasses the uncaughtException handler (F16), and it put a duplicate MB→bytes conversion in server.ts (F18).
guidance_note: When moving a throwing call earlier in a function, check what catches it at the new position: a synchronous throw near the top of runDaemon goes to the caller's try/catch, not to the process handler registered above it.

evidence: TS rejects 007 and Rust accepts it, which is a real divergence. The reviewer also asked for check-protocol to pin the accept/reject sets. The agent unified the grammar but only connected the vector tables by a comment until F19 forced the check-protocol rows.
guidance_note: When the reviewer asks for drift to be pinned by the build, add the build check in the same fix; a comment saying 'same table' is not a check.

evidence: The original test file imported only DEFAULT_RSS_LIMIT_MB, and the new throwing parser had no TS tests. e322618 added accept and reject vector tests.
guidance_note: When adding a throw-on-malformed parser on one side of a mirror, add its vector test in the same commit, as the other side already had.

evidence: The reviewer itself concedes that both callers catch heapCapMb's throw. The heapCapMb derivation got direct unit tests (F10), and asserting the argv string would test one interpolation's structure, so declining was reasonable.

The async closeLog nulled the stream before the flush, so a late dlog could open a second stream whose write nothing awaited. Replacing the stream with a synchronous appendFileSync removes the window. It also made dlog throwable on every call (F15), dropped mkdir self-healing (F27), and drew three perf objections (F14, F17, F23).
guidance_note: When swapping a sink's mechanism (stream to sync append), list the old mechanism's implicit guarantees (errors are async rather than thrown, the dir is re-created on reopen) and keep each one deliberately.

evidence: This is the third duplicate of the F2/F7 grammar divergence (`+10` and `007`). It was resolved by the same unified grammar in e322618.

Sync appendFileSync is on the per-render path, which is true. The agent measured ~70 µs per line, about 0.035% of the 200 ms budget, and the buffered alternative is what lost the death line. The tradeoff exists only because of F12's sync-append fix.
guidance_note: When a fix moves I/O onto a hot path, put the measured cost in the commit or the comment so the next round doesn't flag it.

evidence: In e322618's dlog, `fs.appendFileSync` runs with no try. A throw from it inside server.ts's uncaughtException handler escapes before shutdown(). The stream it replaced reported write failures asynchronously. 2e07fcb wrapped the append, but not logPath() (F29) or the stderr fallback (F24).
guidance_note: When a function is called first inside crash handlers, make it total in the same commit: wrap every statement that can throw, including path resolution and the fallback channel, not just the main write.

evidence: e322618 moved `rssLimitMb(process.env)` to the top of runDaemon as a bare synchronous call. That throw lands in index.ts's try/catch, whose stderr the detached spawn discards. Before the move, the throw was in onListening's callback and reached the uncaughtException handler, which logged it. 2e07fcb added a local try/catch with dlog plus shutdown(1).
guidance_note: When relocating a throwing call to satisfy an ordering finding, route its failure explicitly through the same death funnel at the new site instead of assuming the process-level handler still catches it.

evidence: This duplicates F14 in the same round. The measured ~70 µs per append does not support the latency concern, and buffering would bring back the lost-death-line defect.

e322618 removed the `* 1024 * 1024` conversion from realLimitsDeps in limits.ts and re-wrote it in server.ts as `rssLimitMb(process.env) * 1024 * 1024`, so the unit conversion left its owner. 2e07fcb exported rssLimitBytes from limits.ts.
guidance_note: When hoisting a derivation to a new call site, hoist a call to the owner's function, not the inline arithmetic that used to live in the owner.

evidence: The e322618 replies claimed 'the same vector table runs in' both suites, but the two tables were independent literals joined only by a comment, which F9 had asked to be pinned. 2e07fcb added memberSet rows to check-protocol.
guidance_note: When claiming two runtimes share a table, make the build diff the tables before writing 'same table' in the reply.

evidence: 2e07fcb's catch comment said 'stderr is the one channel left', but both spawners route stderr to /dev/null. The agent corrected the comment in 609aa2f and declined a second emergency sink, which is a defensible scope call.
guidance_note: When writing a comment that names a fallback channel, check where that channel goes in the production spawn path before claiming it carries anything.

evidence: The flag points at 2e07fcb, but the `const MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024` literal was introduced in e322618's new test/daemon-log.test.ts, which was F3's fix. 609aa2f exports MAX_BYTES and imports it.
guidance_note: When a new test needs a module's threshold, export the threshold rather than copying the literal.

evidence: JS trim() strips U+FEFF and Rust str::trim() does not, yet e322618's comment called the grammar 'the TS grammar verbatim — trimmed'. 609aa2f removed trim on both sides, so the grammars are identical by construction.
guidance_note: When unifying two grammars, drop any step whose semantics differ by runtime (trim, Unicode classes) rather than calling it 'verbatim'.

evidence: This is the third perf objection to the sync append. The long-lived-fd suggestion adds reopen-on-rotate and ENOENT state to save part of a measured ~70 µs, so declining it is justified.
guidance_note: When pushing back on a recurring perf finding, put the measurement in a code comment at the site so later rounds can read it.

evidence: 2e07fcb's catch calls `process.stderr.write` unguarded, so dlog can still throw (EPIPE), contrary to the 'never throws' claim F15's fix introduced. 0d9d2c3 wraps it, with a test.
guidance_note: When making a function total, guard the catch block's own I/O as well as the try body.

evidence: The refuse-before-side-effects ordering added in e322618 and 2e07fcb had no test. 0d9d2c3 added test/daemon-boot-refusal.test.ts, which spawns the real daemon and asserts exit 1, the log line, and no socket. That is better than the reviewer's pure-helper suggestion because the claim is about ordering.
guidance_note: When a fix asserts an ordering of side effects, ship a test that drives the real binary and checks the side effects that must be absent.

evidence: 2e07fcb's ACCEPT memberRegex `("[^"]*", ?\d+)` captures the formatting between the fields, unlike the normalizing num() and lit() rows. The risk is low because both formatters agree today. 0d9d2c3 captures two groups and joins them with `=`.
guidance_note: When adding a row to a drift checker, canonicalize the captured value the way the existing rows do instead of comparing raw source text.

evidence: In e322618, currentBytes runs mkdir only while bytesWritten is null, and rotate sets it to 0, so a removed state dir is never recreated. The old stream path re-ran mkdir at each reopen. 0d9d2c3 nulls the counter in the catch, which self-heals on the next call, earlier than the reviewer's rotation-based fix.
guidance_note: When replacing lazy-init-on-reopen with a cached counter, preserve the re-init path for the case where the resource disappears.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive. The MB×2^20 multiplication existed in the original PR's realLimitsDeps (`rssLimitMb(process.env) * 1024 * 1024`); 2e07fcb only moved it into rssLimitBytes, and 0d9d2c3 did not touch it. Inexactness near 2^73 bytes changes no `rss >= budget` comparison, and the 2^53 bound exists for the exact heap-cap integer.

2e07fcb's dlog calls `const filePath = logPath();` before the try, and logPath reaches os.homedir(), which can throw. This is the third gap in the 'never throws' fix after F24. 4224037 moved it inside the try.
guidance_note: When making a function total, start the try block at the function's first statement instead of wrapping only the visibly risky call.

narrative: Round 0 raised 13 real findings: a grammar divergence reported four times, an ordering bug, and an async log race. The agent fixed them in one commit, e322618. That commit seeded most of the remaining 16 findings. Replacing the log stream with a sync append made dlog throwable, which took three more rounds (F15, F24, F29) to close; it also lost mkdir self-healing and drew three perf objections that were rightly declined. Hoisting the budget parse made its throw silent (F16) and leaked the unit conversion (F18). The 'verbatim' shared grammar was still not verbatim (F22), and its tables were not machine-pinned (F19, F26).
guidance_observations: The 'dlog never throws' invariant was established over three rounds, one throwing statement at a time; a single pass checking every statement in dlog would have closed it in round 1.
Replies repeatedly asserted things the code did not yet back ('the same vector table', 'grammar verbatim', 'stderr is the one channel left'), and each assertion became the next round's finding.
The perf objection to the sync append recurred three times because the measurement lived only in thread replies, not at the code site.

evidence: The reduced absolute margin is real, but the reviewer's driver (transcript buffers) is refuted by the agent's measurements: usageCache.size=0, and 186 MB RSS / 52 MB heap with ~20 sessions on this branch. 512 MB was also the pre-#197 budget. The measurements cannot be checked from the packet. no-silent-failure does not fit a sizing choice; the backstop-that-never-fires argument is about the backstop's usefulness, not about a swallowed failure.

The agent explains that go-template-js resolves `{{ template }}` at evaluation via ctx.defines, so declaration order does not affect resolution, and the feared breakage was not real. A forward-reference test was still missing even though the bundled default relies on it, and 4c02dcd added one.
guidance_note: When a refactor changes how definitions are assembled, add a test for every resolution shape the bundled config already relies on, forward references included.

evidence: The test double-gcs, warms up before reading `before`, and measures a delta. The agent reports five runs of 1.22–1.24 MB against a 4 MB bound and a 29.4 MB regression, and CI runs without coverage. The proposed comparative bound is the same assertion with a looser number.

narrative: Round 0 raised three advisory findings. Two were declined with live measurements, and one was answered with a forward-reference test. Rounds 1–4 produced no findings; each re-review followed another push and approved. No finding came from an earlier fix.
guidance_observations: Answering pushbacks with measured numbers (RSS, heap, per-run variance) closed those threads without re-litigation in later rounds.
Four zero-finding rounds came from re-pushes after round 0. That is review cost not tied to any finding, so it does not count as avoidable here.

evidence: onReload handed out the mutable CacheEntry. 7c74408 typed it as `Readonly<CacheEntry>`. That is shallow and does not block method calls such as `watcher.release()`, which F7 then found.
guidance_note: When narrowing what an observer can do, enumerate the reachable methods as well as the fields; Readonly<> stops assignment, not calls. Prefer an allow-list Pick of what the observer reads.

evidence: `for (;;)` with only a per-round cap meant Jest's timeout pre-empted the `finally` cleanup. A MAX_ROUNDS cap that throws at ~12.8 s, below 30 s, fixes it without bringing back a wall-clock deadline, which is consistent with the PR's own goal.
guidance_note: When a retry loop's terminal failure is 'the test runner times out', bound it below the runner's timeout so cleanup runs.

evidence: getOrCreate called reloadInto, which calls onReload, before `entries.set`, so a throwing observer stranded live handles outside the map. 7c74408 swapped the order. The swap was shipped without a test (F8) and left the eviction check after the throw point (F10).
guidance_note: When reordering steps so a throw leaves state reachable, re-read every step after the throw point to see what it now skips, and add a test that throws there.

evidence: `this.next(entry); mutate();` run in one synchronous block and the reload reads disk synchronously, so any reload that resolves round N+1's resolver ran after round N+1's write. A false pass cannot occur. The stale-resolver shape existed in the original for(;;) loop, not only after F2's fix.

This is the same claim as F4, from a sibling thread. The guarantee is 'a reload ran after my latest write', and synchronous subscribe-then-mutate ensures it whichever round's event triggered the reload.

The render-path truncation exists for bar width, and this log line is the only untruncated copy of the error. Volume is one line per debounced fs event, so filling 5 MB needs thousands of broken saves. Truncating would lose the diagnostic.

7c74408's `Readonly<CacheEntry>` still let an observer call `entry.watcher.release()`. 85fbd69 omitted watcher, which closes that one handle but is a deny-list that left `state.registry.dispose()` reachable (F9).
guidance_note: When a reviewer shows that one handle leaks through a type, sweep the type for every other method-bearing field instead of omitting just the named one.

evidence: 7c74408's reorder exists to close the throw-strands-entry and reentrancy cases, and it shipped with no test for either. 85fbd69 added both tests and confirmed they fail with the old order.
guidance_note: When a fix exists to close a named failure case, ship the test that reproduces that case in the same commit.

evidence: `Readonly<Omit<CacheEntry, "watcher">>` still exposes `state.registry.dispose()` and the validator disposers. 4480e3e switched to an allow-list Pick of the outcome fields plus `state: Pick<DslRenderState, "config">`, which closes future handles as well.
guidance_note: When defining an observer's view of internal state, build it as an allow-list of the fields it reads, not a deny-list of handles.

evidence: After the reorder in 7c74408, a throw from reloadInto skips the eviction check that follows, so the cache can grow past maxEntries. Before the reorder, nothing was inserted on a throw. 10c8dfb orders the steps insert → evict → load, which beats the suggested try/finally, and adds a test at capacity.
guidance_note: When moving a mutation ahead of a step that can throw, move the invariants that bound that mutation ahead of it too.

narrative: Round 0's three findings were all real. Two of the fixes started chains. The observer-type narrowing went Readonly, then Omit watcher, then an allow-list Pick, over three rounds; the allow-list would have ended it in round 0. The insert-before-reload reorder shipped without a test (F8) and skipped eviction on a throw (F10). The round-1 race claims (F4, F5) and the log-size claim (F6) were correctly declined with sound reasoning.
guidance_observations: The observer-view type took three rounds because each fix closed only the specific reach the reviewer named; the agent's final allow-list reasoning was available in round 0.
Fixes for a named failure case (reentrancy, a throwing observer) were pushed without the test that reproduces the case, which cost a round.
